title: The Last Supper
reflectionQuestion: Jesus gave his friends a way to always remember how much he loved them. What helps you remember someone you love when they are far away?
kidSafetyNotes: NEW anchor (Easter, secondary/short-only). Completes the Easter path (1832 Palm Sunday -> 1850 Last Supper -> 1821 Cross -> 1812 Empty Tomb). Per Adam (2026-06-18): 'Jesus gave his friends a meal to remember his love' -- TENDER REMEMBRANCE ONLY, NO body/blood explanation. So the bread + cup are framed simply as a way to 'remember me / remember that I love you / I am always with you'; no doctrine of the elements. Jesus' coming death is kept OFFSTAGE and gentle -- 'he would have to go away from his friends for a while' (not 'he was about to die'); flag references_departure_softened. Warm not somber: lamplight, friends close together, peaceful. Connects to today (people still share bread + cup) and lands on the CHILD being loved + Jesus near (not-alone spine). Distinct Easter scene (the meal), no overlap with 1832/1821/1812. 'God'/'Jesus' throughout, no Yahweh. VOICE_JOHN_BELOVED (tender, loving -- Johannine intimate register; John was at this table).
